card: Updates `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` (test networks only) so mempool policy checks only enforce consensus script verify flags instead of rejecting non-standard script executions. Currently, testnet nodes configured to accept non-standard transactions still reject spends with uncompressed SegWit keys or opcodes reserved for future soft forks (such as OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS). The patch also makes the validation context explicit in CheckInputScripts and enforces at compile time that standard verify flags subsume block script flags.
evidence: PR description: 'This PR changes `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` so that it also skips the non-mandatory script checks, allowing txs that (eg) use OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS into the mempool. This remains only available on test nets.'

Commit 9b6342e5d2: 'Prepare for updating -acceptnonstdtxn to allow txns that violate STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS but not MANDATORY_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS by checking the non-mandatory flags with node that enforces standardness.'
problem: On test networks, `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` allows transactions with non-standard templates or sizes into the mempool, but policy script checks still enforce standard script flags (such as disallowing `OP_SUCCESS`, `OP_NOPx`, or uncompressed keys in SegWit). This prevents developers from testing soft fork upgrades and other non-standard script execution behaviors through the mempool on testnets.
scope_notes: Touches validation callers and unit tests by adding an explicit `CheckInputScriptsFor` enum argument to `CheckInputScripts`, and introduces a `consteval` helper class `StandardScriptVerifyFlags` in `src/validation.cpp` to statically check flag inclusions.
summary: Modifies `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` (test networks only) so mempool policy script checks enforce only potential consensus script flags rather than full standard script verification flags. In doing so, it replaces the heuristic flag-mask check in `CheckInputScripts` with an explicit enum distinguishing block from mempool validation, and adds compile-time checks ensuring standard script flags remain a superset of block script flags.
